txt: He chuckles. "There are things even a cop can't fix, my man. There's no helping an absence, you know?"
He rubs his jaw. "Then what's your deal here?"
His eyes grow wide and he hyperventilates. "Is she *dead*? Don't tell me she's..."
It's hard to say. His gaze wanders southwest -- down the street that goes beyond the horizon...
Out of old habit he still snaps his fingers at you -- but then stops immediately, realizing what he's done. He does not want to talk to you.
That breath of his isn't calming down. "Man, I need to take a breath here, excuse me..."
The man taps his fingers rhythmically against his arm.
Then he gives them to you. "Her lorry is still here. Down, past the statue of Filippe," he waves toward the monument. "The cabin is green. You can get in there with these. That's all I know."
There's a pause and a sigh. Then he turns his eyes to you. "What about you, cop-man? You missing someone?"
"*Merciful*. Downright merciful -- you cops keep exercising *that* muscle and people will be more willing to cooperate, you know."
"A friend? An acquaintance. I don't know... She was the only person in this damn jam I could talk to. She's someone I don't want to rat out to the law, okay?"
"A great white ghost? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage."
"A little. She's okay. Troubled but -- a nice person. She left last week. Left me the keys to park her lorry if the jam should break."
"A sense of surprise there ain't more bodies hanging from more trees."
"A young-ish woman. Gruff, but... in a cool way."
"Ah, man, me and narcotics go way back." He folds his hands behind his head and leans back. "Had some good times surfin' the psychic waves of my own consciousness, you know?"
"An ex-wife?"
"Analysin' the fundamental structural and psychological conditions of being stranded in the midst of a sea of motor lorries and their sad, despondent chauffeurs."
"And she didn't do it -- believe me. If it's something *bad* then she didn't do it. Didn't know her for long but I know people."
"And she didn't do it, believe me. If it's something *bad* then she didn't do it. Didn't know her for long but I know people."
"Anything else I can help you with?"
"Anything else?" He thinks. "Yeah, this ain't really my area of expertise. I just do my job and get paid. I have things to do and places to be. All of us do."
"Back already?" He grins at you.
"Black reverb? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage."
"Blue and violet, dyed." He answers reluctantly. "It was violet when she got here. Blue before she went."
"But... thanks for this. It's nice to talk to someone. And I know it wasn't easy to ask." He smiles. "I hope you find your way through your own troubles."
"But..." he pauses, letting the memory dissipate. "Those days are behind me. There are other addictions in my life now. Why the inquiry, my man?"
"Can't even get a few jokes past you, my man." He grins. "I've got another haul of FALN cargo. Mostly sporting goods. Tracksuits and that kinda thing."
"Cool, cool... We all want to know each other, know each other's woes and all -- but people, man, they have *slippery* souls..."
"Damn, I always warned her to watch herself... man, nothing to do now, I guess."
"Damn, I don't wanna..." He looks you straight in the eye. "Please just let it go. Whatever she did, it can't be that bad. She's not a bad person, I know that much."
"Dang," he grunts, unable to suppress his reaction. "That's some *great* shit. You came up with that yourself?"

"Deora-of-the-Seven-Seas. It's on the other end of Le Caillou, pretty much -- on another island, called Laurentide, off mainland. We've got a little place there. I can almost hear my kid laugh, when it snows..."
"Don't be a stranger." He gives a salute with two fingers.
"Don't tell me. Just back off and don't talk to me again, okay? I can't talk to cops anymore. I can't be involved in this shit. "
"Dunno. Whatcha need?"
"Everyone's a critic, man." He waves you off. "It's okay. I've been here a whole week already."
"Excuse me?" He emerges from the reverie.
"Feels like forever, like I was born on this here roundabout and this was all I ever knew. Just me and the metal and the tyres, the oil and the fumes of mazut..."
"Fine. I don't want to be a butcher. And I don't want to be a knight either. I just wanna be a person who can sleep at night. A little fame wouldn't hurt too."
"From another... planet," he finishes and turns to you: "Hey there."
"Fuck it," he shrugs. "I'm a bad guy now. There's things more important than holding a grudge. It's okay -- you've been through enough."
"Fuck, man... Go grill someone else with these questions, okay? There are plenty of drivers here who couldn't stand her. Or were *afraid* of her. They'd be more than happy to rat her out."
"Fuckin' A! Seems I got you all wrong. Cops aren't much known for their artistic sensibilities these days."
"God damn, this shit is too intense for me..." He looks at his feet, steadying his breath. "I don't wanna know, man. I don't wanna know if she even got away..."
"Good eye, my man. Yup, she's an old one, but reliable." He gives the side of the lorry a friendly knock. "Me and her spent a *long* time together."
"Good luck with that, my man. Ain't easy being you, but hey, you're still breathin', right?"
"Gotta guard the stuff -- bosses don't look kindly on missing cargo. And it gives me time to work on my rhymes."
"Hah, no. I'm joking, my man." He grins. "FALN runs a nice, clean business. This haul of cargo is mostly sporting goods. You know, tracksuits and that kinda thing."
"He ain't one of us drivers -- I know that. All accounted for. Otherwise, I haven't really asked about that. Been wastin' time right here. Keepin' busy."
"Hello again, my man." He greets you. "What's on your mind?"
"Here." He takes a keyring from his pocket -- then looks at it before giving it to you. In silence...
"Hey man, that's serious criminal talk. Are you trying to pull some sort of an... entrapment thing on me?"
"Hey, officer. Got a minute?"
"Hey, that's just what I heard. Old wives' tale. So -- what next?"
"Huh?" Sudden financial duties snap him out of his daze. "Oh. No, I ain't got any money. They don't want to pay for unfinished work."
"Hunted? By what?"
"I *told* you not to go after her! I TOLD you." He's hyperventilating. "What happened? Is she... is she..."
"I am a gander and a hunter and a gatherer, feel like a traveller..." The man mutters to himself, accenting the beats as he goes.
"I bet you are."
"I didn't, man -- I told you, I was *hoping* it's not her. That she wouldn't be mixed up in it."
"I don't believe you."
"I don't want to talk about that..." He shifts around, suddenly uncomfortable, then looks away.
"I feel for you, my friend. It's bad enough to *know* who you miss... missing like that doesn't feel like it has much of an upside."
"I feel for you, my friend. It's good to miss someone. I like it. Knowing there's something *more* than what I have with me here."
"I get ya. When they really *click* it makes the world seem manageable. Good to be on the same page." He gives you a thumbs up.
"I heard the rumours. I saw the others drivers looking at me *strange* when we talked. And she told me too -- that she's had a violent life. But I wasn't afraid of her, more like *for* her."
"I just can't, man. I'm not *naive*."
"I miss my family. They're all I have, my wife... a second kid on the way... waiting all the way in Deora. And here I am, stuck in this shit, so far from home."
"I'm okay, man. Just... the jam's got me down. The fumes, the chemical rainbows, the tarpaulin stretched on the frames and the dull engines off..." The man recedes into his daze of words.
"I've heard talk there's a company rep in town too. Like... a strike negotiator type. They'd know what's up. Precise demands and so on."
"I... I thought you were a different kind of cop." Something breaks in him as he stares into your eyes.
"I... uh... saw you poking around in lady driver's lorry. She in trouble?"
"It's a bad habit. You ought to quit, too."
"It's a traffic jam for the ages. Harbour gates up the street are shut tight. No explanation given. Workers on strike. Scabs agitatin'. An all-around clusterfuck."
"It's good talking to someone. I know it wasn't easy to say those things, so..." He smiles. "I hope you find your way through your own troubles."
"It's good to meet a fellow poet -- someone with an appreciation for *real text*. The others here, see, they don't really *get* it."
"It's like... whatever's going on over at the docks. Workers got a blockade set up. Making demands. No way in or out."
"It's never a good time to quit." He shakes his head. "You just gotta sit it out, friend."
"It's snitching, man. I know what it is."
"It's that bad?" He lets out a whistle, looking about ten years older suddenly. "Man, what should I do... what should I do to help her?"
"It's the Jam, my man." He motions toward the sprawl of lorries with a sweeping gesture.
"Just *happened*?" His eyes grow wide and he hyperventilates. "Is she *dead*? Don't tell me she's..."
"Just messin' with you. It's cool, you're an okay guy, for a cop."
"Last Friday." He blinks, his eyes half-empty now.
"Look, man, I try to stay away from the criminal underbelly of Revachol. I'm a guest here. You really need to find another man to probe with those questions."
"Look, man, fuck off, okay? Fuck off and let me have a panic attack. I don't need to know about this shit anymore. I can't talk to cops any more..."
"Make way for the master poet!" He greets you with a nod.
"Makes sense? It sucks is what it does."
"Man, I was hoping it isn't gonna be her..." He bites his lip. "All I can say is -- she isn't around here anymore; she isn't some evil drug-trafficker; and I don't know where she is."
"Man, I was hoping she'd catch a break." He shakes his head. "All I can say is: she isn't around here anymore. She isn't some mastermind evil-doer. And I don't know where she is."
"Man, nothing's troubling me. Just the usual lorryman tropes and hopes: the road and the rhymes. This jam ain't helping either..." He looks around.
"Man, relax. I quit, been clean for some time. There are some commitments you have to honour." He looks at you with compassion in his eyes.
"Man, what a day... I missed out on most of the action, but I heard it was quite the encounter." He nods thoughtfully. "Had a strong sense of *finality* to it."
"Man, who even knows? It's like a legal contract, but also a bond between spirits... Every one is different, that's all I can say."
"Man." He sighs. "I don't know what to say. Not much anyone can do... there's no helping an absence, you know?"
"Maybe I should just keep my head down and work on my rhymes while I can."
"Maybe it is. We're doing our best to keep ours together. I *hope* it's not, but you never know..." A pause. "Thanks for the dark words, I guess. I'll make sure they don't come true."
"Maybe you should. Cops don't get paid much and the hours are long. Plus, you can get shot. Why not?"
"Maybe. But not *another* person's life."
"Meanwhile, we're all stuck here in long haul limbo for days upon days upon days..." He glances south, down the road. "Upon days."
"My man, you're alive!" He assesses the situation. "Almost... kind of... sort of alive."
"Nah, man, I was telling you the truth. I really didn't think it'd be her. She's okay. Sorta troubled but, still -- a nice person."
"Nah. I need to think my own thoughts now. Pray forgiveness for my sins. Go check your cabin..." He adds quietly: "I hope it gets you something. Helps someone."
"Neat -- for carrying large quantities of cargo a long distance. These FALN tracksuits need to find their way to the kids way out in Uamrao and L'Iramburde somehow..."
"No matter, it's a fine stanza. You're not so bad after all, for a cop."
"No matter. Great verse is like that sometimes -- ephemeral. You might not look it, but seems you have some literary chops. Maybe there's hope for me yet!"
"No, my man, you asked for my cigarettes." There's sadness in his voice; he doesn't seem offended, though.
"No. I don't know."
"Nope. Don't smoke." He nods toward the big lorry behind him...
"Not me, man, no way. I don't need any trouble. Shit's bad enough anyway. This jam's got folks up in arms and I'm afraid it's headed toward a conflagration."

"Not my thing. Chasin' transient pleasures is a drag these days. I prefer the examined life now -- thinkin', reflectin', observin'." He glances down the road toward the horizon, a glint of... something in his eyes.
"Not unless they've illegalized sports equipment while I was on the road."
"Nothing, man. We just talked a bit -- about life and stuff..." He looks to you. "So, is she in trouble or what?"
"Nothing. We just talked a bit -- about life and stuff. She left me her keys, so I can park her lorry if the jam broke..." He looks to you. "So, is she in trouble or what?"
"Nothing." He smiles. "I'm just messing with you, man. Don't mind my idle verbosity."
"Now it's turning into a... kind of a..." He searches for the right expression. "Snow limbo, man. What's on your mind?"
"Oh look..." As you approach he instinctively averts his eyes. "It's the cop who turned me into a bad person."
"Oh man, that's like... a load off my mind. All that stress was messing up my rhymes."
"Oh, high-grade narcotics. Illegal fire-arms. Stuff like that."
"Oh, you know..." The thought lightens him up. "Tommy Le Homme's gonna be a musician. *Sprechgesang*, but with beats. I've got lot of free time on the road to hone my craft."
"Okay, man, I believe you." He gives you a funny look.
"Okay..." He seems a little apprehensive.
"Okay..." His eyes smile. "But this is my last one. And it's a bad habit. You should quit before both of us have lung cancer."
"Planar hunter? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage."
"Right, man -- *anew*." He adds with a smile and a nod: "The phoenix at the traffic jam."
"Right. But really -- no bullshit. That's great stuff. I sorta wanna know if it's yours..."
"She left them to me. Because she trusted me... So I can get it out of the way when the jam breaks loose. Otherwise..." He doesn't finish the sentence.
"She's got the *darkness* in her. That young person's darkness when you think it's all over. And you're looking for a way *out*."
"Shoot." He pauses, then chuckles all of a sudden. "Sorry man, didn't mean it like that. Ask away."
"Silent communion, that's good..." He's transfixed by the words.
"Sinister presence? Wow... that sounds really bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage."
"So what's next? You headin' back to Jamrock now? Talk is local Union muscle were behind it all, I'd reckon the case is closed... even if it kinda turned into a shitshow."
"So, tell me... what do you need?"
"So, you do realize entrapment doesn't work if you announce you're going to do it in advance?"
"Some of the other drivers do, though. There's still a few around, waiting for the Jam to disperse. Or waiting for the sweet release of death."
"Some pretty wild stuff, I hear. Like a giant new power-crane and half the company? I forget *what* exactly. Good on them, I guess..."
"Sorry?" His eyes grow wide and he hyperventilates. "Is she *dead*? Don't tell me she's..."
"Still -- a shadowy figure. That sounds pretty bad. I hope that doesn't happen to my marriage..."
"Still better than me, I guess -- told you there's plenty of others who'd tell on her." He leans in. "But... is she in trouble?"
"Still here, stuck in this damn jam, my man." The man greets you with a smile. "What's up?"
"Stuck in the rain in a traffic jam, man. What's on your mind?"
"Sure man, no problem... and thanks for this. It's good to talk to someone. I know it wasn't easy to ask." He smiles. "I hope you find your way through your own troubles."
"Sure, man, if you say so..." It doesn't look like he believes you. "But look, man..."
"Thank god I *don't know*. People here call her 'the lady driver.' She kept her name a secret. From me, too. Now I see why."
"Thank you, friend." He sighs. It's a big sigh of relief. "Wow, this makes me feel like I should pick up smoking again... Would help with my rhymes too."
"Thanks for this. It's good to talk to someone. I know it wasn't easy to ask, so...." He smiles. "I hope you find your way through your own troubles."
"Thanks for this. It's nice to talk to someone. I know it wasn't easy to ask, so...." He smiles. "I hope you find your way through your own troubles."
"That's brutal, man. But, you know... Time will..."

"That's how it always is with you, isn't it? All part of the investigation..." He shakes his head. "The girl's *troubled* -- if you hunt her down, she may not survive it. I can't have that on my conscience."
"That's probably for the best. You keep your job to yourself -- with a job like yours, you *have* to."
"That's... uhm..."
"The bosses, man."
"The way it worked. The trouble it was giving her."
"Then what are you trying to accomplish?"
"They usually get shipped to Graad and the Occident. Though we've been making headway in the Iilmaraan market lately."
"They want to keep that money flowing in, my man." He makes a 'ka-ching' sound.
"They're more often into fists than rhymes, see. Let alone *honesty in verse*."
"This rockin' beauty?" He points at the lorry with his thumb. "Sure is, like a rash you can't get rid of. You interested in heavy duty cargo machinery?"
"Tommy L'Homme was taken." He shrugs in a what-can-you-do manner. "My real name is Jerry Lefitte -- Tommy's way better."
"Umm... if you say so, officer." He gives you a cautious thumbs up.

"Us lorry drivers. Camionneurs. A few still hang around here waiting for this mess to end. Most have scurried off somewhere. To get drunk, or high. Or laid." He smiles awkwardly. "Not that I blame 'em, really."
"We are what we are. And you're a cop."
"We're pals and all, but I can't just freely hand out the merchandise. The bosses won't be happy."
"Welcome back!" He gives you a knowing nod. "The days ain't going by any faster, believe me."
"Well. You've given *me* some hope, I guess!" He gives you a thumbs up.
"Well..." He sighs. "It looks like it did *now* -- but we didn't talk about that. We talked about life, you know. She talked about her mind..."
"What's it *like*? Good. And bad. An ache that brings you joy." He smiles warmly. "I think of them a lot. I dream up these silly scenarios, in great detail. Of living with them... it comforts me."
"What?" He looks up. "But I *told* you she's my friend! Please don't make me give her up, detective. Get someone else. There's a *ton* of drivers here..."
"What?"
"Whoa." He leans in, his eyes bright with attention. "What else?"
"Whooh. Almost gave me a heart attack..." He sighs with relief. "Yeah, I *really* need to start smoking again."
"Whooh... good on her. And good on *you* too -- better focus your efforts on the bad guys. Mercs and such. Plenty of baddies to go around..."
"Whooh... good on her. And good on *you* too, my man. That's..." He looks for the words...
"Yeah -- you too. Be safe, detective."
"Yeah, imagine -- it's been a whole week already." He snickers.
"Yeah, it sure ain't good for me -- or you. I'd spare a coin or two for a city cop down on his luck. If I had, say, *four* myself."
"Yeah, maybe I should just keep my head down... and work on my rhymes while I can."
"Yeah, must be -- your job's to know all those *little* things isn't it? While my job..." he pats the back of the lorry, "is to deliver tracksuit trousers."
"Yeah, yeah -- exactly."
"Yeah, yeah, I get that and it's cool. But..."
"Yeah. I guess I owe you an apology for thinking otherwise. And again -- *great* shit." He gives you a thumbs up.
"Yeah... In marriage you never know if you're doing the right thing. I *hope* we're doing our best to keep ours together, but -- anything can happen. Look, man..."
"Yeah..." He doesn't know what to say, so he just repeats: "Yeah-yeah. I get it. These are *your* rhymes, they're from your life. Doesn't matter if they're robust, they're honest. So... thanks man."
"Yeah..." He makes a half-hearted salute.
"Yes, it's like... trying to trick a person into doing something criminal that they'd never do."
"Yes, which is why I don't want to *snitch* on her."
"You could also check the kiosque down the street. Frittte." He points towards the harbour. "With three t-s. Revachol is weird..."
"You don't *really* think so."
"You lost your gun? Oh man, that's bad news. Especially here, in Martinaise. I hope you find it soon before things turn foul."
"You sure are, my man." He nods emphatically.
"You're not gonna put a bullet in your head if you blow it, are you? 'Cause she's on the *edge*, man."
